about.title: Rocklin Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Placer County residents rely on a handful of hospitals and clinics serving the Rocklin area, and most visits go fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, the harm can follow you for years. California treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — strict notice periods, expert review requirements, and a capped category of damages all come into play under MICRA. If you or a family member suffered an unexpected complication after care in Rocklin, it's worth having someone look closely at the medical records and timeline. Our team doesn't charge any fee to review your situation; we can explain, in plain terms, whether what happened may amount to malpractice under California law.

items.title: We Understand the Filing Clock
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovery of the injury, capped at three years from the incident, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice — timing we can help track carefully.

items.title: Expert Review Matters
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always required to support a malpractice claim, and our team works with the right resources to evaluate whether the standard of care was actually broken.

items.title: Clear-Eyed About the Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California law places a statutory cap on non-economic damages that adjusts upward each year, and we can walk you through what that realistically means for a case like yours.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Rocklin — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine carries inherent risk, so a poor result alone isn't enough — there has to be evidence the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. We can review your records to see whether that standard was met.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does Rocklin's location in Placer County affect where my case is handled?
items.answer: Cases are typically filed in the county where the care occurred or where the provider is located, which for many Rocklin residents means Placer County courts. We can confirm the right venue once we know where your treatment took place.

items.question: Who do I work with?
items.answer: We handle medical malpractice claims directly and work on a contingency-fee basis, so there's no cost or obligation to discuss whether your situation might qualify for a claim.
